review: The hymn is the marriage of the Lamb: 1:1–4 is Eph 5:32 (סּוֹד גָּדוֹל) with Rev 19:7 and Eph 1:22–23, 2:1–6 is Matt 25:6 with 1 Thess 4:16–17 (בָּאֲוִיר) and 1 Cor 15:51–52, 3:1–4 is Rev 19:7–8 with Ps 45:15, and 4:1–4 is Titus 2:13 with Rev 22:20.

The chorus is printed as a block of six lines between stanza 1 and the rest, and the corpus records the shape as 4/6/4/4; the payload keeps the chorus as its own stanza of six, since the print marks it [القرار].

1:3–4 keep the two appositions of the Arabic (the assembly as the Bride, Christ as the Lord of majesty) on two lines instead of merging them, because the stanza's whole content is that identification.
2:4 בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר — the Arabic بِصَوْتِ بُوقٍ is the trumpet; the Hebrew uses שׁוֹפָר, the horn of Exod 19:16 and 1 Thess 4:16, so the assembly's rapture is Sinai's assembly again.
